# Positioning

Where Spwn stands against what a person uses today instead, for anyone writing a comparison, a
pitch or an answer to "how is it different": the category it refuses, the four alternatives and
what each costs. What Spwn is, in one sentence, is [the vision](../blueprint/vision.md#the-definition)'s
and is not restated here.

## The alternatives

<Group id="alternatives" title="What a person uses today" intent="define" fold>

<Alternative id="by-hand" gives="you know every line" costs="you are the bottleneck: what gets built is bounded by your hours" />

<Alternative
id="one-big-agent"
gives="speed, and one place to ask"
costs="the only safety is its instructions; one context holds everything, and you stop knowing what it did"
/>

<Alternative id="managed-platform" gives="someone else runs the agents" costs="your context, machines and credentials live in their place, worked in their method" />

<Alternative id="unrelated-tools" gives="each tool is good at its part" costs="each keeps its own copy of your context, and you are the integration between them" />

</Group>

<Figure id="two-costs" form="quad" shows={ref("growth/positioning#alternatives")} x="scale" y="authorship" caption="Each costs either scale or authorship." />

Each costs either scale or authorship. Spwn's answer is to keep both: the work goes to agents, the
decisions stay with you, on your machines, from one place for each fact
([the stack](../product/stack.md)).
